chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Khalid and al-Husayn ibn Saeed — both — from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Yahya al-Halabi, from Muhammad ibn Marwan, from Sa'd ibn Tarif, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever recites ten verses during a night will not be recorded among the heedless; whoever recites fifty verses will be recorded among those who remember God; whoever recites one hundred verses will be recorded among the devoutly obedient; whoever recites two hundred verses will be recorded among the humble and fearful; whoever recites three hundred verses will be recorded among the successful; whoever recites five hundred verses will be recorded among the diligent strivers; and whoever recites a thousand verses — a qintar of raw gold will be recorded for him. The qintar is fifteen thousand mithqal of gold, and the mithqal is twenty-four qirat — the smallest of which is like the mountain of Uhud, and the largest of which is what is between the sky and the earth.'

key_terms.الخاشعين: The humble and fearful — those with deep reverence for God
key_terms.الذاكرين: Those who remember/mention God — habitual practitioners of dhikr
key_terms.الغافلين: The heedless ones — those negligent of God's remembrance
key_terms.الفائزين: The triumphant/successful ones — those who attain salvation
key_terms.القانتين: The devoutly obedient — those in constant worship and submission
key_terms.المجتهدين: The diligent strivers — those who make great effort in worship
key_terms.قنطار: Qintar — a large unit of measure used metaphorically for immense heavenly reward
key_terms.مثقال: Mithqal — a traditional unit of weight (~4.25 grams)

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for reciting Quran verses at night according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) relays a hadith from the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) enumerating the spiritual rewards of nightly Quran recitation. The hadith presents a graduated scale — from ten verses to one thousand — assigning each level a distinctive spiritual category (from 'not heedless' up to earning an immense heavenly reward). The elaborate description of the qintar reward in terms of gold and cosmic scale would have struck the original audience as an emphatic image of divine generosity for those who regularly engage with the Quran.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Muhammad Bin Khalid and Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Al Nazar Bin Suweyd, from Yahya Al Halby, from Muhammad Bin Marwan, from Sa’ad Bin Tareyf, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’farasws having said: ‘Rasool-Allahsaww said: ‘The one who recites ten Verse during a night would not be Written as being from the neglectful ones; and the one who recites fifty Verses would be Written as being from the Zakireen (Oft-Mentioners of Allahazwj); and the one who recites one hundred Verses would be Written as being from the contented ones; and the one who recites two hundred Verse would be Written as being from the fearful ones; and the one who recites three hundred Verses would be Written as being from the successful ones; and the one who recites five hundred Verses would be Written as being from the strivers. And the one who recites a thousand Verses, there would be Written for him a Qintar of gold nuggets. The Qintar is fifteen thousand Misqaal of gold, and the Misqaal is twenty four Qiraat, the smallest of it being like the mountain of Ohad, and the largest of it being what is between the sky to the earth’.
en.sarwar: 5. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Muhammad ibn Khalid and al-Husayn ibn Sa’id all from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from Yahya al-Halabi from Muhammad ibn Marwan from Sa’D ibn Tarif from abu Ja’far (a.s.) who has said the following:

“The Messenger of Allah has said, ‘One who reads ten verses from the Holy Quran in a night he is not written of the neglectful people. If one reads fifty verses, he is written of those who speak of Allah. If one reads one hundred verses, he is written of the pleading people before Allah. If one reads two hundred verses, he is written of those who express humility before Allah. If one reads three hundred verses he is written of the successful ones. If one reads five hundred verses, he is written of those striving for the cause of Allah. If one reads one thousand verses one Qintar of Tibr, gold will be his reward. A Qintar is equal to fifteen thousand Mithqal of gold. A Mithqal is equal to twenty four Qirat and the smallest Qirat is of the size of the mountain of ‘Uhud and the largest equals to the size of space between earth and the sky.”’
